# Tanya's Sprint Retro

Tanya: "We shipped the async decision widget. Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter. The Zephyr integration was the key unlock."

evidence.quote: We shipped the async decision widget.

observations.why: Flat declarative reporting a completed action; no ratification language or performed settling that would lift it to decision, no hedging that would lower it to notion.

evidence.quote: Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter.

observations.why: Unhedged factual assertion with a superlative; stated as fact ready to defend but no performed ratification or operational rule to reach decision.

evidence.quote: The Zephyr integration was the key unlock.

observations.why: Confident causal attribution stated flatly, but still an argued position rather than a settled rule or performed ratification — claim, not decision.
The verb 'shipped' performs completion and delivery of work, appealing to competence as the good realized.
Superlative framing of velocity as a record achievement appeals to self-enhancement — standing and winning as the good.
Naming an integration as the 'key unlock' frames capability and mastery as the decisive enabler — competence as the appealed-to good.

evidence.quote: We shipped the async decision widget.

observations.why: Completed action naming a specific artifact; attention on what happened, actual and concrete.

evidence.quote: Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter.

observations.why: Reported metric from the past, settled and specific with a named figure and timeframe.

evidence.quote: The Zephyr integration was the key unlock.

observations.why: Past-tense characterization of a named integration as the decisive factor; actual and concrete.
The Zephyr integration is spoken of AS a lock mechanism — 'unlock' frames a software integration as a physical key turning, a thing-as-another-thing figure.
The 'we' pronoun enacts communal-sharing — the team as an undifferentiated body that shipped together.
Velocity measured in points and ranked against quarterly output frames work as proportional, quantified output — market-pricing's cost/benefit register applied to team performance.
Framing an integration as the 'key unlock' casts it as the highest-leverage input — proportionality reasoning about which contribution yielded the outcome.

payload.rationale: This sprint retro touches three graph regions: the anti-Slack positioning narrative (the async decision widget is the product embodiment of that thesis), the Zephyr integration position and its blocker resolution (the doc names Zephyr as the key unlock), and the velocity/KPI observations with the metric-anchoring style observation (the doc repeats the 23-point velocity claim). I expanded Narrative_AntiSlackPositioning's children to surface the product-category, anti-pattern, target-market, and pricing positions that give the passes the framing context. I included Sample_Sprint4Retro_20260322 so the passes can recognize this as a new retro entry against the prior one rather than minting duplicates. No areas were deliberately excluded — the document is short and squarely within the mapped territory.
